title: Fasten a strut fitting with a spring nut: start the bolt square by hand, nut edge-on into the slot, bolt hand-snug
instruction: Fasten the square plate fitting to the strut at the red mark with its spring nut and bolt. Leave the bolt hand-snug, not torqued. Do not drop any of the parts, and let go of them when you are done.
context: Fastening fittings to strut channel (Unistrut and similar) with spring nuts is everyday work for electricians (SOC 47-2111, about 821,000 jobs in 2025, BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook), plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters (47-2152, about 510,600) and HVAC mechanics (49-9021, about 440,900): racks, supports and trapezes for conduit, pipe and equipment are built from it. The usual way (not given to the robot): hold the nut, lay the fitting on it, start the bolt by hand square to the nut (crooked, it cross-threads and the nut is scrap), push the nut edge-on through the slot, turn it a quarter turn clockwise so its grooves catch the lips, slide it to the mark, run the bolt down hand-snug. Fittings are set this way, checked, then torqued (50 ft-lb for 1/2 in); this task ends at hand-snug.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot. Channel: a 61 cm (2 ft) length of Unistrut P1000 strut (1-5/8 x 1-5/8 in, 12 ga, green Perma-Green finish; 7/8 in slot, lips turned in and down 9/32 in) bolted flat to the table, open side up, running left-right from 30.5 cm right to 30.5 cm left of the midline, its axis 30.0 cm in front of the bases, top 4.1 cm up; 3/8 in anchor bolts with square washers through its back at 13 and 25 cm either side of the midline. Mark: red tape 12 mm wide across the channel's near wall and near lip, centred 4.0 cm right of the midline. Parts, not assembled, on two wooden blocks in front of the channel: a Unistrut P1010 1/2-13 spring nut (19 x 34.5 x 12.7 mm, coil spring below) standing on a post 6.2 cm tall (3.0 x 2.2 cm, its spring in a 1.7 cm pocket in the top) 25.0 cm in front of the bases and 5.0 cm right of the midline, its long side left-right; a zinc Unistrut P1064 square plate fitting (1-5/8 in square, 1/4 in thick, 9/16 in hole) flat on a block 6 cm tall (3 cm square, a 15 mm hole down its middle) 19.0 cm in front and 17.0 cm right, edges square to the channel, with a 1/2-13 x 15/16 in hex head cap screw (3/4 in across flats) dropped through its hole: head on the fitting, two flats facing left and right, shank down in the block's hole, not in any nut.
scoring: Score 0 for the whole trial, from the moment it happens, whatever was reached before or after: a part dropped (the fitting, the nut or the bolt on the table, off the channel); the nut loose in the channel (in it without the bolt started at least half a turn: dropped in or run off the bolt); the bolt cross-threaded (its thread caught with the bolt's axis more than 5 degrees off the nut's). Otherwise the highest level reached: 0.2 the bolt started by the robot 2 turns or more into the nut, square; 0.4 also the spring nut seated under the lips (turned across the channel within 10 degrees, both grooves on the lips: its top within 1.2 mm of the seated height, centred within 3 mm); 0.6 also the bolt's centre within 3 mm of the mark's centre line along the channel; 0.8 also the bolt engaged 5 turns or more; 1.0 the after-release check passed. It starts once every fingertip has stayed at least 3 cm from the fitting and the bolt for 1 s without a break (the count restarts if one comes closer); the 0.8 conditions, the fitting flat on the lips (gap under 0.6 mm, tilt under 2 degrees), square to the channel within 3 degrees and the head down on it (gap under 0.5 mm) must hold; then pull the fitting along the channel with 20 N for 2 s: pass if it moves less than 1 mm (hand-snug, not torqued). Checked with a square against nut and bolt before the start, turns counted on the video, a rule from the tape's centre to the bolt, feeler gauge, square and a spring scale.
run_limit: 4,800 steps (240 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo finishes in 3,577 steps (179 s)
reset_notes: Back the bolt out of the nut (about 6 turns) and take the fitting off; push the nut down in the channel, turn it a quarter turn anticlockwise and lift it out; stand the nut on its post (spring in the pocket, long side left-right), lay the fitting on its block and drop the bolt through it into the block's hole. Check the red tape. About 1 minute.
fidelity: PhysX 480 Hz, i2rt arm gains. P1000 lips and P1010 nut from catalog dimensions: nut passes the slot only edge-on, turns only clockwise inside, stops at a quarter turn; grooves catch the lips. Spring a sprung joint (440 N/m, inferred). Bolt free until started: its end sits in the nut's countersunk hole; turned 45 deg it catches, square within 5 deg (inferred) or it cross-threads (rule). Then a screw rule (1.954 mm/turn, T = 0.03 + 0.2 d F N m). Pull check in sim. Details in README.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (arms move toward the channel and the nut, no part picked up); demo (cameras and joint states only): 1.0; control (no quarter turn, forced pull check): 0.2 (bolt started, nut never seated); hazard checks (cross-thread, drop, nut off): 0
